title: Every Game Awards Game of the Year Winner Since 2014
description: Every Game Awards Game of the Year winner from 2014 through 2025, from Dragon Age: Inquisition to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, with year-by-year context.
body: The Game Awards has presented one main Game of the Year winner at every show since the event launched under that name in 2014. This page tracks that single annual prize. It is different from broader GOTY totals, which combine awards from many publications, readers and ceremonies. Neural Critic’s [most-awarded-games explainer](/stories/games-with-most-game-of-the-year-awards/) covers those aggregate counts; this article is the clean historical record for The Game Awards itself.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: The Game Awards 2014 imagery accompanying Neural Critic’s year-by-year history of Game of the Year winners.

contentBlocks.text: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 won The Game Awards 2025 Game of the Year prize. The official awards organization also recorded wins for the game across Game Direction, Narrative, Art Direction, Score and Music, Independent Game, Debut Indie Game and RPG, while Jennifer English won Best Performance for her work in the game. The result made Sandfall Interactive’s debut one of the most dominant single-game nights in the event’s history.\n\nNeural Critic also reviewed [Clair Obscur: Expedition 33](/stories/clair-obscur-expedition-33-review/).
contentBlocks.caption: Clair Obscur’s 2025 victory capped a night in which Sandfall’s debut won across direction, narrative, art, music, performance and RPG categories.
contentBlocks.heading: 2025 — Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 accompanying the 2025 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive

contentBlocks.text: Astro Bot won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2024. Team Asobi’s platformer also won Best Game Direction and Best Action/Adventure, giving Sony’s mascot-focused release the ceremony’s top honor in a year that also featured Balatro, Black Myth: Wukong, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth and Metaphor: ReFantazio among the major contenders.
contentBlocks.caption: Astro Bot’s top prize confirmed Team Asobi’s platformer as the standout winner of the 2024 ceremony.
contentBlocks.heading: 2024 — Astro Bot
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Astro Bot accompanying the 2024 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Team Asobi / Sony Interactive Entertainment

contentBlocks.text: Baldur’s Gate 3 won The Game Awards 2023 Game of the Year prize after a year defined by unusually broad critical acclaim for Larian’s role-playing game. The win capped a ceremony in which the game’s reactive storytelling, party-based design and player freedom had already made it one of the year’s central awards-season favorites.
contentBlocks.caption: Baldur’s Gate 3 turned its broad critical momentum into The Game Awards’ top honor in 2023.
contentBlocks.heading: 2023 — Baldur’s Gate 3
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Baldur’s Gate 3 accompanying the 2023 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Larian Studios

contentBlocks.text: Elden Ring won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2022. FromSoftware’s open-world action RPG expanded the studio’s established approach to exploration and progression into a much larger structure, and its victory placed it at the center of the 2022 awards season.\n\nFor more, see Neural Critic’s [Elden Ring review](/stories/elden-ring-review-monumental-open-world/) and [beginner’s guide](/stories/elden-ring-beginners-guide/).
contentBlocks.caption: Elden Ring’s 2022 win gave FromSoftware its second Game of the Year victory at the ceremony after Sekiro in 2019.
contentBlocks.heading: 2022 — Elden Ring
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Elden Ring accompanying the 2022 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: FromSoftware / Bandai Namco

contentBlocks.text: It Takes Two won The Game Awards 2021 Game of the Year prize. Hazelight’s co-op adventure stood out in a field that included Deathloop, Metroid Dread, Psychonauts 2, Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart and Resident Evil Village, giving a cooperative-focused game the event’s top award.
contentBlocks.caption: It Takes Two’s 2021 win put a co-op-first adventure at the top of a field spanning several very different genres.
contentBlocks.heading: 2021 — It Takes Two
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from It Takes Two accompanying the 2021 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Hazelight Studios / Electronic Arts

contentBlocks.text: The Last of Us Part II won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2020. Naughty Dog’s sequel also collected multiple major category wins at the ceremony, including Game Direction, Narrative and performance recognition, making it the defining awards result of that year’s show.
contentBlocks.caption: The Last of Us Part II’s Game of the Year win headlined a ceremony where it also took major direction, narrative and performance honors.
contentBlocks.heading: 2020 — The Last of Us Part II
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from The Last of Us Part II accompanying the 2020 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Naughty Dog / Sony Interactive Entertainment

contentBlocks.text: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice won The Game Awards 2019 Game of the Year prize. The result gave FromSoftware its first TGA Game of the Year win, three years before Elden Ring earned the studio another top-prize victory.\n\nNeural Critic’s [Sekiro review](/stories/sekiro-shadows-die-twice-review/) looks at why its focused design still stands apart.
contentBlocks.caption: Sekiro’s 2019 victory marked FromSoftware’s first Game of the Year win at The Game Awards.
contentBlocks.heading: 2019 — Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice accompanying the 2019 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: FromSoftware / Activision

contentBlocks.text: God of War won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2018. Santa Monica Studio’s reinvention of the series took the top award in an especially competitive year that also included Red Dead Redemption 2, which won several other major categories during the ceremony.
contentBlocks.caption: God of War took the 2018 top prize in a year when Red Dead Redemption 2 collected several other major awards.
contentBlocks.heading: 2018 — God of War
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from God of War accompanying the 2018 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Santa Monica Studio / Sony Interactive Entertainment

contentBlocks.text: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild won The Game Awards 2017 Game of the Year prize. Nintendo’s open-world reinvention of Zelda also won Best Game Direction, reinforcing its position as one of the defining releases of the Switch launch era.
contentBlocks.caption: Breath of the Wild paired its 2017 Game of the Year victory with Best Game Direction during the Switch’s launch year.
contentBlocks.heading: 2017 — The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild accompanying the 2017 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Nintendo EPD / Nintendo

contentBlocks.text: Overwatch won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2016. Blizzard’s team-based multiplayer shooter also received the event’s Best Game Direction and Best Multiplayer honors, reflecting how quickly it became one of 2016’s biggest competitive and cultural releases.
contentBlocks.caption: Overwatch’s 2016 victory reflected the game’s rapid rise as one of that year’s defining multiplayer releases.
contentBlocks.heading: 2016 — Overwatch
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Overwatch accompanying the 2016 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Blizzard Entertainment

contentBlocks.text: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt won The Game Awards 2015 Game of the Year prize. CD Projekt Red’s RPG became one of the defining releases of its generation and remains a major reference point in wider discussions about all-time Game of the Year award totals.
contentBlocks.caption: The Witcher 3’s 2015 win helped establish it as one of the generation’s defining role-playing games.
contentBlocks.heading: 2015 — The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt accompanying the 2015 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: CD Projekt Red / Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment

contentBlocks.text: Dragon Age: Inquisition won the first Game of the Year award presented by The Game Awards in 2014. BioWare’s RPG therefore opens the modern TGA record, which is why this list begins in 2014 rather than folding in awards from earlier events with different names and structures.
contentBlocks.caption: Dragon Age: Inquisition opened the modern Game Awards record as the ceremony’s inaugural Game of the Year winner.
contentBlocks.heading: 2014 — Dragon Age: Inquisition
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Dragon Age: Inquisition accompanying the inaugural 2014 Game of the Year winner entry.
contentBlocks.subtitle: BioWare / Electronic Arts

quickRead: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is the latest completed Game Awards GOTY winner, taking the 2025 prize.
Astro Bot won in 2024, Baldur’s Gate 3 in 2023 and Elden Ring in 2022.
The modern Game Awards record begins with Dragon Age: Inquisition at the inaugural 2014 ceremony.
conclusion: The Game Awards list is simple by design: one top Game of the Year winner per ceremony, beginning with Dragon Age: Inquisition in 2014 and currently ending with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 in 2025. That makes this page a useful reference, but it should not be confused with broader “most GOTY awards” records, where many outlets and reader polls can contribute to a single game’s total. For the current season, Neural Critic’s [2026 Game of the Year watchlist](/stories/game-of-the-year-2026-watchlist/) tracks the race before the next ceremony. We will update this history after each future Game Awards show.
conclusionHeading: The Game Awards GOTY record is one prize per year
